Topic: Impact of COVID-19 on Health Worker Practices

Clues (max 200 words): 
1. "My duty increases, I use to treat patients without gloves but now I don’t do that."
2. "Whenever I see any of my staffs with mask trying to treat a patient, I always stop the individual and caution him/her put on the mask."
3. "So we have become used to it so much that now when am giving treatment, one of them will be standing near me."
4. "It brought awareness to the health workers and also it had almost wanted to cause commotion among the health workers."
5. "We just give injections with our bare hands. It came to a time now that we no longer do that."

Reasoning (max 150 words):  
The clues indicate a significant transformation in health worker practices due to COVID-19. The shift to mandatory PPE usage and increased vigilance reflects a heightened awareness of infection control. Health workers have adapted their interactions and established new protocols, as seen in their cautioning each other about mask usage. The emotional stress and adaptation challenges are evident, as the pandemic has altered workplace dynamics. Overall, these clues demonstrate a systemic shift in health worker practices motivated by the pandemic's threat, contrasting sharply with pre-COVID norms.

Topic: Patient Access to Health Services During COVID-19

Clues (max 200 words): 
1. "The patients’ inflow reduced. Because they were afraid of the sick."
2. "They prefer going to the pharmacy to buy drugs."
3. "They used to say: 'don’t go to that hospital.'"
4. "When they hide from the government hospital we the peripherals thought that they will come here, they never come."
5. "We went to them in their communities, although when we go there they refuse to accept us."

Reasoning (max 150 words):  
The clues collectively illustrate the decline in patient access to health services during the COVID-19 pandemic. The reduction in patient visits is primarily driven by fear of infection, which influences their behavior toward seeking care. The stigma surrounding healthcare facilities leads patients to avoid hospitals entirely, opting instead for pharmacies and further complicating service delivery. This reluctance is compounded by community outreach efforts that fail to gain acceptance. Together, these factors highlight the systemic barriers to accessing health services during the pandemic, underscoring the need for trust-building in healthcare interactions.

Topic: Changes in Health Facility Operations Due to COVID-19

Clues (max 200 words): 
1. "We put everything in place. That table over there, we tied a red rope round it. That was the triage place."
2. "That index case... He said: 'let us observe the PPEs.'"
3. "We have this thermometer. Everything is done there before you go to that table [the registration table]."
4. "We didn’t change any service. We continue all our serves because a patient will not come and because of covid-19, you refuse to render to him/her a service."
5. "We were all alert, because one; if you are not alert, if you refuse to abide by the rules and regulations, you will be infected."

Reasoning (max 150 words):  
The clues emphasize operational changes within health facilities in response to COVID-19. The establishment of triage systems signifies a new approach to patient flow and symptom screening. The focus on PPE usage and temperature checks reflects a commitment to infection control measures. Despite maintaining service delivery, the methods of providing care have adapted to ensure safety. The heightened vigilance among staff indicates a comprehensive operational overhaul necessary for managing the risks associated with the pandemic, showcasing a proactive response to an unprecedented health crisis.

Topic: Emotional and Psychological Impact on Health Workers

Clues (max 200 words): 
1. "Everyone was worried. You don’t know the status of your patients."
2. "It came to a time where we avoided one another."
3. "We used to exchange spoons when eating, but there we were, no one wants to get close to the other."
4. "The only support was our salaries."
5. "We said even if it’s incentive, give it to us."

Reasoning (max 150 words):  
The clues highlight the emotional and psychological toll of the COVID-19 pandemic on health workers. The pervasive anxiety regarding patient health statuses creates a constant state of worry. Social distancing measures lead to a breakdown of camaraderie among staff, further exacerbating feelings of isolation. The lack of adequate psychological support and reliance solely on salaries during this stressful period points to systemic neglect of mental health needs. The desire for incentives emphasizes the need for recognition and support mechanisms to help health workers cope with the emotional strain experienced during the pandemic.

Topic: Legacy of the Ebola Outbreak on COVID-19 Response

Clues (max 200 words): 
1. "Although the reason we didn’t register many victims is because of the knowledge we gained during the Ebola outbreak."
2. "It brought awareness to the health workers."
3. "All that helped us this time. But for the Ebola, we had no prior experience."
4. "The experience we got during the Ebola, is what helped us in this Covid."
5. "If we hadn’t got the Ebola outbreak and the experience from it, many people would have died during this Covid."

Reasoning (max 150 words):  
The clues highlight the profound influence of the Ebola outbreak on the response to COVID-19. The lessons learned during Ebola significantly improved preparedness for COVID-19, as indicated by the reduction in registered victims. Increased awareness and vigilance among health workers demonstrate that previous experiences directly shaped current strategies and operational protocols. This historical context underscores the importance of learning from past health crises to enhance response capabilities and ultimately save lives during future outbreaks, showcasing the critical role of experience in public health management.

2. "We prepared a box, this, for emergencies, everything; face shield, masks, goggles, the gown hand sanitizers, apron."
3. "Everyone was worried. You don’t know the status of your patients, not even the colleague you are working with."
4. "If you are not alert, if you refuse to abide by the rules and regulations, you will be infected."
5. "We put all modalities in place."
6. "Anyone who comes, goes there. They go there as they come. They use to screen people there before coming to us."

Reasoning (max 150 words):  
The clues indicate significant adaptations made in response to COVID-19. Increased duties and strict adherence to PPE usage illustrate a heightened awareness of infection control. The preparedness with emergency supplies demonstrates proactive measures taken to ensure safety. The acknowledgment of fear among health workers highlights the emotional toll of the pandemic. Emphasizing alertness and compliance indicates the critical importance of following protocols to safeguard health. The implementation of screening procedures further illustrates systematic changes aimed at minimizing viral transmission. Together, these clues capture the multifaceted adaptations necessitated by the pandemic.

Topic: Healthcare Resource Management During COVID-19

Clues (max 200 words): 
1. "There was a small amount of increment compared to the previous one."
2. "No increase in cost."
3. "We ask them to pay on the bases on how we buy the drugs from the pharmacies."
4. "As a result of the Covid, we didn’t experience any shortage of drugs or medical supplies."
5. "They had given us forms that have the names of our PHUs written on them to make requisitions, when needed."

Reasoning (max 150 words):  
The clues highlight the management of healthcare resources amid the pandemic. The slight increment in funding suggests adjustments made, though they remain insufficient. Stability in costs indicates some operational aspects were maintained, yet the burden on healthcare financing persists. Reliance on pharmacies for drugs points to challenges in supply chain management. The absence of drug shortages demonstrates effective resource management practices in place. The structured requisition process reflects strategic planning to ensure necessary medical supplies remain available during the crisis, showcasing an adaptive approach to resource management in turbulent times.

1. "The Covid-19 brought awareness to the health workers and also it had almost wanted to cause commotion among the health workers."
2. "Whenever I see any of my staffs with mask trying to treat a patient, I always stop the individual and caution him/her put on the mask."
3. "We put all modalities in place."
4. "They use to screen people there before coming to us."
5. "I said, I alone won’t risk my life. This work, since the day you decided to go into medicine, it is just like the soldier, he won’t back down when there is war."
6. "The stress? Everyone was worried."
7. "No support. The only support was our salaries."
8. "We were alert... if you refuse to abide by the rules and regulations, you will be infected."

Reasoning (max 150 words):  
The clues illustrate the healthcare facility's proactive measures in response to COVID-19, highlighting increased awareness among health workers and the need for personal protective equipment (PPE). The implementation of patient screening and the enforcement of mask usage were critical given the heightened risks posed by the virus. Stress and worry among staff indicate that while there was an organized response, it came with emotional challenges. The acknowledgment of inadequate support beyond salaries reflects systemic issues, revealing the need for comprehensive support structures for healthcare workers during health crises, emphasizing the importance of addressing both operational and mental health needs within health systems.

2. "We avoided one another."
3. "No one wants to get close to the other."
4. "We used to exchange spoons when eating, but there we were, no one wants to get close to the other."
5. "The only support was our salaries."

These clues illustrate the mental health challenges faced by healthcare workers during the COVID-19 pandemic.
